_note: casting.json starter (CASTING.md). Fill every <placeholder> (a --go refuses any left), run `casting.py plan`, quote it to the user. Prompts describe what things ARE; never name what must not appear (that pulls the model toward it): such words go in "ban", a build check. Paths are relative to this file; {NAME} expands a snippet from "text" or the built-ins (SHEET, LOCK, KEEP, STATE, FACELESS, GREY, TAIL, PROP_TAIL, PLATE_TAIL, PRE_FACE, PRE_LOC). Entries whose id starts with "_" are templates casting.py skips: rename one (drop the "_") to use it (CASTING.md rules 13-17: a pose sheet, a product sheet per colourway, a vehicle with its rider, an extra, an animal).

text.WHO: <who: one person in plain words, e.g. an East Asian woman of about 40 with light warm skin, short straight black hair, strong dark eyebrows, dark brown eyes and faint laugh lines>
text.WARDROBE: <wardrobe: the one outfit for the whole film, e.g. a plain navy work jacket over a grey T-shirt, dark jeans and white trainers>
text.POSE: <the pose the shots need, e.g. low in an aero tuck on the bike, forearms on the bars>

state-2.prompt: {STATE} <the change, e.g. soaked from the rain: hair wet and flat, the jacket dark with water>. LEFT panel: a front-facing close-up of the head and shoulders, eyes to camera. MIDDLE panel: the full body from the front, the face area left as a soft plain shadow with no features. RIGHT panel: the full body from behind. {TAIL}

costume.prompt: Image 1 is the locked character sheet. A faceless costume detail sheet: {FACELESS} <tiles: e.g. 1 the jacket's collar and badge; 2 the watch on the left wrist; 3 the trainers from the side and from below>. {PROP_TAIL}

props.prompt: Image 1 shows the world these props belong to. A faceless props sheet: {FACELESS} <tiles, each prop front, side and back, and from below when it will be flipped or tumbled: e.g. 1 a small silver laptop, closed>. {PROP_TAIL}

_pose.prompt: {STATE} The same wardrobe and face, with the MIDDLE panel in the pose the shots need: {POSE}. LEFT panel: a front-facing close-up of the head and shoulders, eyes to camera. MIDDLE panel: the full body in that pose, the face area left as a soft plain shadow with no features. RIGHT panel: the full body from behind. {PROPORTIONS} {TAIL}

_product-gold.prompt: Image 1 {REF_PRODUCT}. A faceless product sheet: {FACELESS} <tiles: the product from the front, the side, the back and above, then a close-up of its smallest part>, in this colourway: <e.g. a mirrored gold lens on a matte black frame>. {PROP_TAIL}

_rider.prompt: {STATE} The same person with <the vehicle, e.g. a glossy pink aero road bike> in all three panels. LEFT panel: a close-up of the head and shoulders, the vehicle behind, eyes to camera. MIDDLE panel: the full side view riding it, the face area a soft plain shadow. RIGHT panel: the full body standing beside it, from behind. {PROPORTIONS} {TAIL}

_extra-1.prompt: {SHEET} The person is <one more character, e.g. a man of about 60 with a grey beard in a waxed olive jacket>. {PROPORTIONS} {READS}<one line: who, and what they wear>. {TAIL}

_animal.prompt: A reference sheet for an animal in a film: ONE image with three side-by-side panels of equal width separated by thin gutters, {GREY}. LEFT panel: a close-up of the head. MIDDLE panel: the whole animal from the side. RIGHT panel: the whole animal from the front. The animal is <the animal: breed, size, coat and markings>. Photographic, natural fur and texture, realistic, not a render, no text, no labels, no watermark.

place-1.prompt: An empty location plate, three-quarter view, no people: <the place, its materials, and a clean corridor where the action happens>. <the light, pinned: e.g. low warm sun from the left, cool shadows>. LENS GATE: <where the camera stands, e.g. one metre above the rock, four metres back, looking straight at the edge>; {FOV:35}; ready for a performer to be placed. {PLATE_TAIL}

S01.prompt: {PRE_FACE}{PRE_LOC}<the shot's first frame: framing, where the person is and what they do, expression, light>
